open_points.subject: M30–M34
open_points.text: five correspondences over a closed list that the data provider held as text-to-text maps became tables whose rows name the members themselves
open_points.question: Which correspondence and which two closed taxonomies does each of M30–M34 represent?
options: One distinct row model for each of five named correspondences
A shared row model used by all five tables
Some correspondences share a row model while others have distinct models
open_points.default_guess: Use one distinct row model per correspondence and require each model to name its source and target taxonomies.

open_points.subject: M30–M34
open_points.text: their rows have the records M30–M34
open_points.question: What domain facts does each row carry, including which member or members it names on each side of its correspondence?
options: Exactly one source member and one target member
One source member and a collection of target members
The two members plus additional correspondence facts
open_points.default_guess: Give each row exactly one source-taxonomy member and one target-taxonomy member.

open_points.subject: M30–M34
open_points.text: Like M22–M29 they are the row shapes of tables the generated code reads
open_points.question: Is each of M30–M34 a value model or an entity model, and, if it is an entity, what identifies it?
options: Each row is an entity identified by the pair of members
Each row is an entity with a provider-minted identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat every row as a value whose equality is determined by all of its facts.

witness.initial: A delivered table contains a row connecting one member of each closed taxonomy.
events: The data provider delivers the table.
Generated code reads the row twice in separate operations.
outcomes: Both reads produce the same value with no persistent row identity.
Both reads refer to one persistent entity identified by its member pair or by a provider-minted id.
witness.observer: Code that compares, stores or references correspondence rows

open_points.subject: M30–M34
open_points.question: Who creates each row, and from what authoritative source are its facts and any identity derived?
options: The data provider creates rows from its former text-to-text maps
A release-building action creates rows from specification taxonomies
Registry creates or normalizes rows when it receives provider data
open_points.default_guess: The data provider creates the rows directly from its authoritative correspondences, with Registry assigning nothing.

open_points.subject: M30–M34 tables
open_points.text: became tables whose rows name the members themselves
open_points.question: Are these tables immutable release inputs, replaceable provider datasets, or mutable runtime records, and what event creates, replaces or retires their rows?
options: Immutable for a release and changed only by a new verified release
Replaced whenever the data provider delivers a new table
Rows may be created, changed or removed during normal runtime
open_points.default_guess: Treat each table as immutable within a release and replace it only through a new verified release.

witness.initial: A deployed release reads a correspondence table containing one row.
events: The data provider later changes that correspondence and delivers revised data.
A product action reads the correspondence after delivery but before a new release.
outcomes: The action still reads the release-pinned row.
The action reads the provider's revised row immediately.
witness.observer: The caller whose product result depends on the correspondence

open_points.subject: M30–M34 tables
open_points.text: they are the row shapes of tables the generated code reads
open_points.question: Which product action or actions read each table, and does any product action create or change it?
options: Named read actions consume the tables and no product action writes them
Every action using the relevant taxonomy may read them
A provider-ingestion action creates or replaces the tables before other actions read them
open_points.default_guess: Name the specific consuming actions and state that no Registry product action creates or changes the tables.
